items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1975-11-13
items.q: Earl King, I just helped him out with it.

ctx.x: Let me tell you. In the end. I'm trying to think. After Rip you went with, you did some things for Joe Asanto again. Yeah. And that was about, you did Third House from the Corner. Yeah. And Big Chief. Yeah. And well the Big Chief was a big thing. Earl King said he wrote that. He wrote that. Yeah.

Earl King, I just helped him out with it. Did he come up with the arrangement or did you? Well I had to rearrange some of the things. To fit what I was putting into his song you know. I had to rearrange the beat. And I had to rearrange the breaks. Well Wardell would give me a hand with it because he had to write the music for all the other instruments. I never find nobody could write for me you know. And Wardell's good, he can write for anybody. Oh but me? I don't know.
He sounded pretty good on that. Well I don't have any piano music.

items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: play Big Chief, the song that she wrote. Professor Longhead, yeah.

ctx.x: Yeah. The song that we put together. So, uh, like I'm saying the producers, they're the one that say, hey, I think, uh, this should be this. And they're going to decide for, uh, millions of people in America. They're going to decide what they will take. Yeah. Can you play? We have to go in about, uh, 10 minutes or so. Can you play a couple more?

Before we have to go? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Just, just the influence of my writing. Yeah. Cool. Why don't you play, why don't you play Big Chief? Try, play Big Chief, the song that she wrote. Professor Longhead, yeah. I can't put it off. I want to make me shine. I can't do it with my song. I can't do it with my song. I can't do it with my song. I'm gonna do a thing I want Be bitchin' I feelin' good Be bitchin' I got a plan I'm gonna do a thing I want My bad boy gets my part My bad boy is who I'm gonna do that…
